upsert.title: Immunotherapy for canine oral melanoma
upsert.center: The Ohio State University Veterinary Medical Center
upsert.status: Actively recruiting — confirmed on Ohio State's current clinical-trials page
upsert.contacts: Blue Buffalo Veterinary Clinical Trials Office — CVM-ClinicalTrials@osu.edu
upsert.funding: Study covers tumor biopsy, two CT imaging sessions, trial-related blood work, viral reagent/injections, immune-cell collection/priming/reinfusion, plus an $800 post-trial incentive; confirm any remaining owner costs with Ohio State.
upsert.notes: Current Ohio State treatment study using intratumoral weakened LCMV followed by collection/expansion of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, with reinfusion if metastatic/progressive disease develops. Public criteria require localized confirmed oral melanoma accessible to injection/biopsy; a randomized control arm does not receive the virus injection but remains eligible for immune-cell collection/reinfusion if disease progresses.

upsert.title: CAR-iNKT cell therapy for canine metastatic osteosarcoma
upsert.center: University of Pennsylvania School of Veterinary Medicine — Comparative Immunotherapy Program
upsert.contacts: Nicola Mason, BVetMed, PhD, DACVIM, FRCVS — nmason@vet.upenn.edu — (215) 898-3996
upsert.funding: Penn Vet states costs associated with the study treatment are covered; confirm current screening and non-study costs during prescreening.
upsert.notes: Phase I B7-H3-targeted CAR-iNKT cell-therapy study for dogs with metastatic osteosarcoma. Penn Vet's official current clinical-trial page is the primary status source; full protocol eligibility requires Penn prescreening.

upsert.title: Radiation plus histotripsy for canine soft tissue sarcoma
upsert.center: UT Southwestern Veterinary Research and Oncology Clinic
upsert.status: Actively recruiting — confirmed on UT Southwestern VROC current trials page
upsert.contacts: Paige Neumann, Research Study Coordinator — 214-645-6221; VROC@UTSouthwestern.edu
upsert.funding: VROC states owners are generally responsible for treatment, tissue and data-collection costs; some grant-supported treatments may be subsidized. Confirm the current estimate with VROC.
upsert.notes: Open-label pilot treatment study combining radiation with image-guided histotripsy for naturally occurring canine soft tissue sarcoma. The registry describes radiation once weekly for three weeks with histotripsy twice weekly 24–72 hours after radiation, plus serial biopsies and monitoring.
